premise.claim: KEP-502 motivation (docs-only PR, premise check run as motivation-claims verification): RBG/RIS/RI lack status.phase today; RBG declares Progressing and RollingUpdateInProgress but the built-in controllers never write them; RBG Ready reflects all-replicas readiness without revision convergence; RIS/RI record operation failures as FailedScale/FailedUpdate conditions.
premise.patchedComponent: keps/502-workload-status-model/ (design document only; no API/controller changes in this PR)
premise.evidence: C5 green at head (results/unit-l1-at-head.txt): no json:"phase" tag in any of the three v1alpha2 status types; zero writes of RoleBasedGroupProgressing / RoleBasedGroupRollingUpdateInProgress / "Progressing" / "RollingUpdateInProgress" in internal/ and pkg/ non-test Go; FailedScale/FailedUpdate declared in v1alpha2 RIS and RI condition enums and written by statelessmode/reconciler.go:237,251 and instance_reconciler.go:191,235; RBG Ready computed purely from role.Replicas == rs.Replicas == rs.ReadyReplicas (rolebasedgroup_controller.go:783-793) with no revision check, reasons AllRolesReady/RoleNotReady at :796/:804.

findings.note: keps/502-workload-status-model/README.md:275 lists Preparing as a Progressing=True candidate reason, but it is never defined or used anywhere else in the KEP; the KEP's own rule (README.md:130) requires controller-written reasons to be valid and consistent. Fix: define it or drop it from the row.

The KEP introduces RolesNotReady (ChildReadiness family reason for Progressing, README.md:158,276) alongside the retained RoleNotReady (Ready=False reason, README.md:222,278; matches code rolebasedgroup_controller.go:804). Two machine-readable strings on the same object differing by one letter, never called out. Fix: acknowledge the distinction explicitly or rename the family reason.

README.md:413 lists InPlaceUpdateNotReady as an RI aggregated-readiness candidate reason, but the current controller writes InplaceUpdateNotReady (pkg/reconciler/roleinstance/instance_status.go:298, lowercase p) for the RoleInstanceReady condition whose reasons the KEP marks retained/compatible. Case-sensitive mismatch. Fix: match the code spelling or explicitly mark the reason as renamed.

Round 2 (delta f05e1dd..6335eac): the revision rewired RBG recovery derivation to 'lower-level conditions' (README.md:463 'RBG derives recovery facts from lower-level conditions, not a RIS `Recovering` phase'; :502 'RBG transitions use lower-level conditions and recovery facts') but left the Goals item (:70 'Define how lower-level phases and recovery facts trigger RBG phase transitions') and the RoleBasedGroup intro (:211 'transitions based on the current target, lower-level phases, and recovery facts') on the old 'phases' vocabulary. C8 passes at f05e1dd and fails at 6335eac (differential). Fix: align :70/:211 to the conditions vocabulary (or 'phases and conditions'); both wordings verified to flip C8 green. Round 3: Goals (:70) and RBG intro (:211) now read 'lower-level phases, conditions, and recovery facts'; C8 red at 6335eac, green at f622d64 (results/reverify, results/bite-check-round3.txt).

Round 2 late discovery on unchanged text (identical at f05e1dd and 6335eac, so pre-existing, not a revision regression): the RIS Progressing prose (README.md:358) says 'Activity reasons may include `ScalingUp`, `ScalingDown`, and `RollingUpdate`' while the activity/child-readiness family table (:159-165) also defines RIS reasons `Creating` (:162) and `Recovering` (:165). Materiality rose in this round because the revision made RIS recovery reporting load-bearing (:345 'RIS propagates recovery through `Progressing` and `Ready` conditions'). Fix: enumerate all five activity reasons in the prose or state the family table is the complete source; verified to flip C9 green. Round 3: prose now reads 'Activity reasons are Creating, ScalingUp, ScalingDown, RollingUpdate, and Recovering' — the complete family-table set. C9 initially reported STILL-BROKEN only because its anchor phrase 'may include' was reworded to 'are'; C9 re-anchored (accepts both) and re-proven: red at 6335eac, green at f622d64 (results/bite-check-round3.txt).

Copilot round-3 advisory (nit, never gating): the reporting-priority list resolves between reason families, so heterogeneous Activity facts (one role Creating, another Recovering, another updating) left the RBG Progressing=True reason underdetermined. Round-4 delta (da818779) adds the within-Activity precedence Creating > Recovering > ScalingOrUpdating with rationale, the one-dominant-reason + all-activities-in-message rule, and test-plan coverage of the concurrent combinations. C10 red at f05e1dd/6335eac/f622d642, green at da818779. Round 5: the fenced precedence, one-dominant-reason rule, and rationale are intact at 0b7285b7, but the redesign dropped the unit-test bullet covering the concurrent heterogeneous combinations (Creating-over-updating/recovering); C10 part 4 goes red. Tracked as F13-concurrent-activity-coverage-regression (this manifest) rather than reopening this finding. Round 5: match split — C17 guards the design content (fenced list, one-dominant rule, rationale; green at head), while C10 retains the full round-4 contract including the test-plan coverage clause, which the redesign regressed (tracked as F13-concurrent-activity-coverage-regression).
findings.status: fixed-at-da818779 (design content intact at head; test-coverage clause regressed, tracked as F13)

findings.note: Round-4 consensus open item (Codex F11 = Claude Q4). Round 5 fixes it: RIS Activity precedence for Progressing is stated (Creating, Recovering, RollingUpdate, ScalingUp/ScalingDown; recovery outranks active update and scaling, update outranks scaling) plus the retained recovery-overlap test bullet. C12 red at da818779 (and all earlier heads), green at 0b7285b7.

Round-4 consensus open item (three-source: Codex F12, Claude cross-critique, Copilot C4471100373). Round 5 e09cb647 scoped Creating to initial creation; 0b7285b7 restated the mapping definitionally at BOTH layers: Creating when a required child/RI does not yet exist and is being created; Recovering when an established child/RI is being repaired or replaced. A mid-recovery group is therefore not reported as Creating under the stated definitions, and the round-4 :495 bullet that prescribed the misfire is gone. C13 green at head; residual derivation ambiguity (absent-replacement-child matches both clauses; no statement of how 'established' is derived, esp. post-restart) tracked as F14 (nit).

Round-5 revision regression (C10: pass@da818779 -> fail@0b7285b7, same valid contract check): the redesign (0b7285b7) dropped the unit-test bullet covering the concurrent heterogeneous Activity combinations. da818779 had 'During the RBG's initial creation, one role Creating with another updating or recovering uses Creating'; head retains only 'When one role is Recovering and another is updating, RBG uses Recovering. When only update or scaling work remains...'. The precedence design content itself (fenced list, one-dominant rule) is intact; only the test-plan coverage regressed. Mutation fixC (restoring the bullet) flips C10 green. Nit, non-gating.

Round-5 late discovery on new text (the F12 fix as landed): the establishment-based mapping leaves the discriminator implicit. For an absent child being replaced, BOTH clauses apply ('a required child object does not yet exist and is being created' AND 'an established child is being ... replaced'); the KEP never states how the controller derives 'established' from persisted facts, and the restart rule says Progressing.reason is recomputed 'from current facts'. e09cb647 had an explicit lifecycle-stage rule ('after the RBG has entered Running, replacement maps to Recovering') which 0b7285b7 replaced with the terser establishment wording, together with removing the controller-restart test bullet that pinned the outcome. One sentence (e.g. 'an established child is one previously observed, determined from persisted roleStatuses') closes it; mutation fixB flips C16 green. Nit, non-gating.

Round-5 new content introduces a normative contradiction (C15: vacuous-pass@da818779 -> fail@0b7285b7; the clause did not exist before): the common rule (README.md:140) and the unit-test bullet (:510) say the parent writes status.observedGeneration=N together with Progressing=True 'including preCheck failures', while the Accepted semantics (:233) require Progressing=False with the matching incompatibility reason when Accepted=False. Both are normative ('must', 'the parent writes'); no sequencing statement reconciles them. An implementer reconciling a new generation whose preflight fails must guess. Fix: scope the Progressing=True companion to the dispatch case and state that a confirmed incompatibility writes Progressing=False with the matching reason (mutation fixA flips C15 green). Minor, non-blocking.

refutedHypotheses.claim: Reviewer hypothesis during stage 1: 'RIS retains ... rolloutReplacementState' names a field that does not exist in the current API, making the KEP's retained-field inventory factually wrong.
refutedHypotheses.evidence: C1 green at head AND at base 885d655: api/workloads/v1alpha2/roleinstanceset_types.go:201 declares RolloutReplacementState *RolloutReplacementState json:"rolloutReplacementState,omitempty" in RoleInstanceSetStatus. The initial grep that suggested absence ran in a stale checkout at an older commit. All 12 retained fields named at README.md:340-341 and the three preserved RI fields at README.md:415 exist in the current API.
